findings.reason: The protected source retains every maximal repeat-run length, requiring O(n) auxiliary space despite the branch's O(1) requirement. The inert candidate accumulates the replacement total and the only two needed remainder counts during the run scan, so its working storage is constant.

The protected source uses the prohibited local name index for the repeat-run cursor. The candidate uses conventional interview variables n, i, and j while preserving the app-local solve(password) contract.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 420 and its Python strongPasswordChecker surface. The Reference preserves all three strength rules, the three permitted edit operations, all three source examples in order, both constraints, and the source's illustrative weak and strong passwords.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064761682 and matches the protected app-local source's character-class count, maximal-run discovery, short and medium formulas, and modulo-prioritized deletion greedy. The candidate is inert and preserves those decisions while replacing the run-length list with sufficient aggregate counters.

The legal 10-, 25-, and 50-character single-run tiers span 5x and exercise repeat repair plus mandatory deletion. The candidate passes all 12 executions at 0.88x the protected reference runtime; a correct control that walks backward from every character to rediscover its run head passes every output but fails only the runtime verdict at 9.91x.

The Approach exactly describes the candidate's streaming run aggregation, the short and medium length formulas, the one-, two-, then three-deletion marginal-cost order, its exchange justification, and genuine O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary space.

The hash-bound public Reference preserves the complete password-strength model, all three examples and their lack of explanations, both source constraints, the source's operation definitions, and the absence of source visuals or tables.
